newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate Democrat urges regular budget order.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate Democrat urges regular budget order.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Monday Republicans should follow the regular budget process and either offer amendments to President Clinton's budget or offer their own plan for bringing the deficit under control.

"I think the best approach is to start the budget process to allow amendments, to work through the budget in the Budget Committee. That entails negotiation and consultation with the White House as well as Democrats. I don't see any reason why we couldn't get started this week," the South Dakota Democrat said at his regular press conference.
Daschle said he was encouraged by comments made by the Republican chairman of the Senate Budget Committee who said on CNN's Late Edition he felt budget talks could start.

Chairman Pete Dominici, a New Mexico Republican, said that he would offer a Republican alternative budget if Clinton did not make deeper cuts in entitlement programs such as Medicare to balance the budget.
"We can produce a budget. In fact, I will recommend one if we can't get an agreement on entitlements."

Clinton sent Congress a $1.69 trillion budget proposal that cut $98.4 billion in taxes over five years, slashed $100 billion from Medicare health care for the elderly and reached a $17 billion surplus in 2002.
